key_insight: A variationally correct first-order least-squares residual provides a locally reliable error measure for nonlinear physics-informed operator learning under stability and smoothness conditions.
engineering_relevance: For nonlinear mechanics, including compressible Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity, the approach enables surrogate training and inference-time error estimation in a PDE-compliant norm.
method: Establish residual–error equivalence using linearized stability and Lipschitz continuity of the residual derivative.
Train a reduced-basis neural operator in a conforming finite element space using the least-squares loss.
Use solution snapshots only to construct the basis; assemble the loss and its symbolic gradient with a finite element library.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests show that the square root of loss excess tracks error within factors comparable to the linear case, while the operator outperforms grid-based baselines in the PDE-compliant norm.
watch_item: Reliability is conditional: depending on the PDE, equivalence may hold only near a solution branch, and loss excess is defined relative to the finite element solution’s loss.
paper_title: Variationally correct physics-informed operator learning for nonlinear partial differential equations
